Court Bans BYD From Selling Its Land Rover Defender Copycat in Europe
8 photos
Photo: tthg 04 | TikTok
A district court in The Hague banned Chinese automaker BYD from selling its Ti7 SUV in the European Union, ruling that the vehicle infringes on EU design rights. It is happening just a couple of months after BYD's European offices were raided following Jaguar Land Rover’s claims that the Chinese company copied its Defender's design and technology.
The district court in The Hague issued the preliminary injunction banning BYD from selling its Fangchengbao Ti7 in Europe. The preliminary relief judge determined that the seven-seat Ti7 copies " characteristic and distinctive elements of the Defender. "
The report highlighted the resemblence between the two , especially focusing on flat-roof silhouette and boxy appearance of the Chinese SUV, along with the upright proportions and tailgate styling, squared-off wheel arches, and the solid, body-colored panel behind the rear passenger door.
The injunction goes into effect one week after the ruling on November 20, 2026. Beyond banning imports, sales, and advertising across all 27 member states of the European Union, the court also barred BYD from producing the Ti7 at its upcoming plant in Szeged, Hungary, which is slated to begin mass production in early 2027.
Photo: JLR The restriction remains in force until the full intellectual property dispute is resolved. If BYD violates the EU ban, it faces daily fines of €100,000 or €25,000 per vehicle ($27,500), capped at €10 million ($11 million), Reuters reports .
The Dutch court ruled that it does not have jurisdiction over BYD’s affiliate in the United Kingdom. JLR originally initiated the lawsuit earlier in 2026, after BYD listed the Ti7 for order on its UK website, with a price starting at 47,995 pounds ($63,010), which undercuts the Defender by a solid 20,000 pounds ($26,260).
Customer deliveries in the UK are planned to start in January 2027 and are by no means affected by the decision. JLR is expected to file a separate UK design-infringement lawsuit in British courts before those January deliveries begin. In the meantime, a separate lawsuit filed by JLR in Rotterdam, alleging copyright infringement and " slavish imitation ," will proceed independently.
BYD stated that it "strongly disagrees" with the decision, claiming that the Ti7 SUV is the result of independent design work and confirming it will appeal the ruling. JLR noted that the legal proceedings remain ongoing.
Photo: BYD Back in August, court-appointed bailiffs, acting for JLR, seized digital files from BYD’s European offices in Schiedam and Hoofddorp, Netherlands. BYD argued that the seizure was a " fishing expedition " that swept up unrelated data.
On November 12, the District Court of The Hague ordered Jaguar Land Rover to destroy or return documents and digital records seized during the August raid on BYD’s Dutch offices. JLR was ordered to destroy the materials within 24 hours and provide third-party confirmation to BYD. Non-compliance carried a penalty of 50,000 euros ($54,840) per hour, capped at a total of 500,000 euros ($584,400).
JLR has a mixed track record in intellectual property court battles over vehicle styling, with court appearances starting long before the BYD Ti7 was in the making. Back in 2016, after JLR ended production of the classic Defender , billionaire Sir Jim Ratcliffe, now also a shareholder of the Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula 1 Team, alongside Mercedes-Benz and Toto Wolff, offered to buy the tooling and rights to continue to build it.
JLR refused, so Ratcliffe founded INEOS Automotive to build what he saw as a spiritual successor to the original Defender, the INEOS Grenadier . JLR attempted to block the launch of the Grenadier by registering the 3D exterior design of the classic Defender as a trademark in the United Kingdom, but INEOS opposed the applications.
Photo: JLR Both the UK Intellectual Property Office and the High Court ruled against JLR. The court found that the classic Defender’s boxy silhouette was not distinctive enough to function as a trademark, noting that the differences from the utilitarian 4x4s were only noticeable to specialists, not average buyers.
The decision eventually cleared the way for the Grenadier’s production, though JLR did successfully secure the 3D shape trademarks for the classic Defender in the United States. However, the INEOS Grenadier is also marketed in North America.
This happened two years after Chinese automaker Jiangling unveiled the Landwind X7, an SUV closely resembling the Range Rover, marketing it at roughly a third of the price of the British model. The Chinese had actually filed a design patent for the X7 even before JLR patented the Evoque in China, leading to years of patent invalidation fights.
JLR lost the design patent and copyright claims and sued Jiangling Motor Corporation, along with its joint venture subsidiary Jiangling Motor Holding, as well as an authorized Beijing dealership that sold the Landwind X7.
Photo: BYD In 2019, a Beijing court ruled in JLR's favor. The court found that Jiangling copied five distinct exterior features of the Range Rover Evoque, causing consumer confusion, and ordered an immediate halt to sales. Jiangling was also ordered to pay 1.5 million Chinese yuan (171,861 pounds or $224,840) in damages to the British automaker.

Third-Gen 2028 Ford GT Looks Like an Exotic Muscle Car in New Rendering
7 photos
Photo: Instagram | tedoradze.giorgi
There was never a better time to launch a new-generation Ford GT , as something like this would take a swing not only at the real exotic models from the likes of Ferrari, Lamborghini, and McLaren, but also at the high-end versions of the C8-generation Chevrolet Corvette.
The most agile and punchiest production ‘Vette ever adds the ZR1X suffix, and is capable of hitting 60 mph (97 kph) in a neck-snapping 1.89 seconds. It has a 233 mph (375 kph) top speed, runs the quarter mile in just 8.99 seconds at 157 mph (253 kph), and boasts a jaw-dropping amount of power.
With 1,250 hp (933 kW /1,268 ps) and 937 pound-feet (1,270 Nm) of torque available via the right pedal, the Chevrolet Corvette ZR1X is more powerful than yesterday’s hypercars, not to mention a heck of a lot faster. It features the same flat-plane crank V8 as the Z06. The 5.5-liter unit has twin turbos, and is assisted by the same electric trickery as the E-Ray that was recently dropped and replaced with the Grand Sport X.
Therefore, a brand-new Ford GT would need to be extremely powerful if it wanted to try and put the Chevy Corvette ZR1X in its corner. However, realistically speaking, it would probably not come anywhere near the bowtie brand’s hypercar’s specs, as chances are it would be a bit slower, while also costing a lot more. The ZR1X has an MSRP of $231,100, in case you forgot, though it comes with extreme dealer markups that make it eye-wateringly expensive.
Photo: Instagram | tedoradze.giorgi I there such a thing as an entirely new Ford GT in the making as we speak? That would be a no, because the Dearborn-based automaker has not released any information about such a project. Moreover, we haven’t seen any test mules in the open suggesting such a thing, let alone prototypes, and we also haven’t heard anything about a possible MK V.
But why the Mk V and not the Mk III, given that there have been only two generations of the Ford GT, not counting the iconic GT40 from back in the day? Well, there is a GT Mk II, which is a track-only version of the second generation, as well as a GT Mk IV launched to commemorate the company’s win at the 1967 24 Hours of Le Mans.
This model honored the original 1967 car, and was limited to 67 units for obvious reasons. It launched for the 2023 model year, featuring a redesigned carbon fiber body, a long-tail configuration, more space between the axles, and other changes, including the semi-exposed front wheels, a new rear wing, and other stuff. A unique chassis setup was also part of the makeover, as well as a tuned variant of the EcoBoost twin-turbo mill making over 800 horsepower.
However, the Mk III hasn’t been used on a Ford GT so far, so chances are a potential revival of this iconic American supercar might be known as the Mk III. Still, as we already told you, nothing suggests that such a thing is in the making as we speak, and if that is indeed the case, then what is up with the images shared in the gallery? Well, two of them are actually renderings, and while we covered one recently , which focused on the car’s front fascia, we now have a second digital illustration to work with.
Photo: Instagram | tedoradze.giorgi It came from the same pixel artist known as @tedoradze.giorgi on Instagram, and imagines the back end, which definitely sends some S650 Mustang vibes. Why is that? Because of the taillights, obviously, which have been clearly inspired by the ones of the brand’s modern-day muscle car. The CGI-infused supercar features an integrated rear wing, a sporty-looking bumper and diffuser combo, a pair of large exhaust tips, muscular shoulders, and a very sharp-looking profile.
At the front, this rendered new-gen Ford GT looks more like a McLaren than a Ford, in my opinion, anyway, so it definitely needs some more pixel manipulation in order to resemble something that would come from the Dearborn company’s portfolio. The supercar has a white paint finish, double racing stripes running across its entire length, large wheels, and posed virtually next to the iconic first-gen GT at the racetrack.
To be honest, it may eclipse it in the eyes of the average Joe, but most real petrolheads would likely gather around the older machine shortly after taking a quick look at this new one. At least that’s what I would do.
Now, do you think the Blue Oval should invest a serious amount of money in the development of a new-generation GT ? Is this what would Ford really need in today’s challenging conditions? What if the end result would actually look similar, or perhaps identical, to the rendered supercar shared above? Would you praise it or criticize it? Let us know what you think of it by dropping a few lines in the comments box. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Giorgi Tedoradze (@tedoradze.giorgi)

If Pontiac Was Left Alive by GM, This Could Have Been a Current Pontiac Grand Am Sedan – Rendering
6 photos
Photo: jlord8 / Instagram
A certain part of the General Motors fanbase thinks that the largest US automaker should have retired the Buick nameplates instead of the ones from Pontiac – and the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI are certainly entertaining them.
Pontiac, formerly the Pontiac Motor Division of General Motors , was an American automobile brand owned, manufactured, and sold by GM from 1926 until late 2010. It would have been its centennial anniversary last year, but it wasn’t meant to be, as GM decided to pull the plug and focus only on Chevrolet, Buick, Cadillac, and GMC after the big financial crisis of the late 2000s.
Well, that hasn’t boded well for some of the fanbase because, unlike Oldsmobile or Buick, the Pontiac brand was created for a bit of sportiness rather than comfort and elegance. It also had quite a few iconic models along the way, such as the Bonneville, GTO, Grand Am, or the legendary Firebird and its Trans Am variation.
Sure, it also had some duds – the most famous of them all being the Pontiac Aztek. But years after its demise, of course, people only remember their hits, not their misses. Just recently, the famous Ringbrothers again brought Pontiac to worldwide attention after creating, for the 2026 SEMA Show in Las Vegas, Nevada, their latest masterpiece – a convertible GTO based on a five-inch-widened Pontiac Tempest Convertible rocking a 650-hp transformation after more than 5,500 hours of intensive labor.
Pontiac is also a darling of the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI, as it turns out. The latest example comes from Jim, a virtual artist known as " jlord8 " on social media, who loves messing around with all things CGI from the automotive realm, and he dreams of a Pontiac that could have been, if only the brand wasn’t retired back in 2010.
More precisely, the pixel master imagines the continuation of the Pontiac Grand Am as if the mid-size RWD nameplate was still a thing. In the real world, it was offered across five generations with various body styles – two-door fastback or notchback coupe, as well as four-door notchback or fastback sedan. The imagined continuation model is a traditional four-door sedan complete with the signature ‘beak,’ most likely based on the soon-extinct Cadillac CT4 or the surviving CT5 models.
It’s not unnatural for this CGI expert to create such models featuring retired nameplates – check out the gallery, and you’ll also see a Ford Crown Victoria sedan , a Chrysler Sebring grand tourer, a Mitsubishi Galant VR-4 Turbo, or even a MazdaSpeed 6 dwelling alongside the wishful-thinking Pontiac Grand Am. So, what do you think – yay or nay? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Jim (@jlord8)
